sections.normalized_html: A fair die has [MATH: 9] sides labeled with numbers [MATH: 1] through [MATH: 9.] What is the probability of getting a number greater than or equal to [MATH: 6] on the next throw of the die?
sections.readable_text: A fair die has [MATH: 9] sides labeled with numbers [MATH: 1] through [MATH: 9.] What is the probability of getting a number greater than or equal to [MATH: 6] on the next throw of the die?

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Let [MATH: X] represent the number the die lands on. From the problem statement, we know that [MATH: X \sim U \{ 1, 2, \ldots, 9\},] and we wish to compute [MATH: P(X \geq 6).]

In general, if [MATH: X] follows a discrete uniform distribution over a set [MATH: S,] then [MATH: X] has the following probability mass function:

[MATH: {(1)/(|S|),|x ∈ S; 0,|otherwise]

Here, we have [MATH: X \sim U \{ 1, 2, \ldots, 9\},] and the set [MATH: S = \{ 1, 2, \ldots, 9\}] has [MATH: |S| = 9-1 + 1 = 9] items. So, we have

[MATH: {(1)/(9),|x = 1, 2, …, 9; 0,|otherwise]

In [MATH: S,] the items that satisfy [MATH: X \geq 6] are [MATH: 6, 7, 8, 9.] Since there are [MATH: 4] elements in total, we have

[MATH: P(X \geq 6) = 4 \cdot \dfrac{1}{9} = \dfrac{4}{9}.]

Item 2 — Tutorial: Determining When a Discrete Uniform Distribution is Appropriate

Content:

- each [MATH: x\in S] must be equally likely.
